messages.content: My client has been arrested and charged under PPC Section 379 (Theft) and PPC Section 420 (Cheating), and has been in police custody for 14 days without a formal charge sheet. As his defense counsel, what are the statutory grounds under CrPC Section 497 to apply for his post-arrest bail in court?

### Legal Explanation
The client has been arrested and charged under PPC Section 379 (Theft) and PPC Section 420 (Cheating), and has been in police custody for 14 days without a formal charge sheet. According to CrPC Section 497, when any person accused of a non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or appears or is brought before a Court, he may be released on bail. However, the client shall not be released on bail if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years. Since the maximum punishment for the offences under PPC Section 379 and PPC Section 420 is three years and seven years respectively, which is less than ten years, the client may be released on bail.

### Cited Statutory Sources
- Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, Section 497
- Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, Section 379
- Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, Section 420

TITLE: Punishment for theft:
CHAPTER: INTRODUCTION
============================================================

Punishment for theft:
Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment
of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
ACT: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860
SECTION/ARTICLE: 420
TITLE: Cheating and dishonestly Inducing delivery of property:
CHAPTER: INTRODUCTION
============================================================

Cheating and dishonestly Inducing delivery of property:
Whoever cheats and
thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or
to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is
signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall
be punished with imprisonment, of either description for a term which may extend to seven
years, and shall also be liable to fine.
